chapters.title: Threshold
chapters.plain: The lower complex controls entry into a royal architectural program; GIZA treats this as an architectural fact before assigning ritual meaning.

chapters.title: Ascent
chapters.plain: The causeway physically joins lower and upper components. Its constrained route is a testable candidate for processional sequencing.

chapters.title: Upper cult
chapters.plain: The pyramid temple and pyramid form the upper mortuary/cult focus; continuing offering practice belongs to the broader royal pyramid-complex model.

chapters.title: Royal-image field
chapters.plain: Valley Temple finds and the official Khafre statue record make repeated royal imagery a direct archaeological context. Exact statue positions and ritual choreography still require primary plan/findspot parsing.

chapters.title: Marked upper threshold
chapters.plain: The Khafre architrave is reconstructed by the Met as spanning a pyramid-temple court doorway with royal titulary and associated falcon/statue imagery, making the threshold itself a testable symbolic/action node.

chapters.title: Meaning guard
chapters.plain: A designed sequence demonstrates controlled movement. It does not by itself recover the words, theology or intended future audience of the builders.
